correctness.rationale: Uniform 5-adic convergence follows from a 5-divisible factor among each block of five. For j>=10 every omitted-factor derivative term has a 5-divisible factor. The independently evaluated table F(a)=(1,0,1,3,4), F'(a)=(1,3,4,2,4) modulo 5 shows unit slope on all five disks. Difference quotient implies exact valuation equality for inputs in one disk; Hensel digit lifting gives exactly one solution to each target in each matching disk for all k>=1. Even/odd branch signs sum to frequencies (2,3,1,1,3), and complete periodicity gives exact index densities. Exhaustive independent recurrence checks through 5^6 and direct derivative checks corroborate the arithmetic; the proof, not enumeration, covers all k.

value.rationale: A motivated exact arithmetic statistic: complete image and frequency law for fixed-point-free permutation counts at all powers of five. It establishes the smallest fully covered prime and the nonuniform index densities for every residue, rather than recycling known modular periods or reporting a few enumeration levels. The five-adic local-isometry structure is reusable for other congruence questions, but no unproved downstream result is asserted.
